name: SS-31

lead: SS-31 (elamipretide) is a synthetic tetrapeptide that targets mitochondria. It has been developed as a drug for rare mitochondrial disease, and gray-market versions circulate as research chemicals.
In longevity discussions it is promoted for energy and anti-aging. Evidence is from disease trials and animal aging studies; there is no demonstrated cosmetic anti-aging benefit in healthy people.

paras: SS-31 binds cardiolipin in the inner mitochondrial membrane, which is thought to stabilize respiratory complexes, improve electron transport efficiency and reduce reactive oxygen species production.

Reported adverse events in trials are mostly injection-site reactions. Long-term safety is not fully established, and vendor products are unregulated. Any regulatory approval concerns specific rare diseases, not general use.
